## TL;DR

The command palette (`SearchOverlay.vue`) is shared by the header ⌘K pill, the
settings palette and the context palette, so I fixed the palette as one
component rather than per caller. Four classes of problem: focus was lost on
dismissal from the header pill, screen readers could not follow the highlighted
result, keyboard movement could leave the highlight off-screen, and empty or
loading states gave misleading copy. Two new regression suites pin each class
across all three scopes, and the WebKit walk at 375, 768 and 1280 now also
covers the empty-result state.

## Work and rationale

I started from the existing palette QA coverage (`keyboard-shortcuts-qa.test.ts`
in jsdom and `keyboard-shortcuts-qa-browser.test.ts` in headless WebKit), which
already checks overflow, the keyboard legend and the close-button focus ring at
the three widths. The gaps were in behavior and semantics those suites did not
exercise, so I read the component against those gaps.

- **Focus after dismissal.** `closeOverlay` only restored focus when a caller
  passed `returnFocusEl`. Settings and Context pass one; the header pill
  (`SearchBar.vue`) does not, so Escape from the pill dropped focus to `body`.
  Rather than patch the pill, the overlay now records `document.activeElement`
  when it opens and uses that as the fallback. Opening a result passes `null`,
  so the drawer that opens is not pulled back by a stale focus restore.
- **Screen readers.** The input had no link to the listbox or the highlighted
  option, so arrowing announced nothing. It is now a combobox with
  `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`, and rows carry ids. Group wrappers
  are `role="group"` (a bare div inside a listbox is not a valid child). The
  keyboard legend had an `aria-label` on a role-less div, which assistive tech
  ignores; it is now a labelled group.
- **Scroll.** Arrow keys moved the highlight but never scrolled it into view in
  the capped list. A watcher calls `scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" })` on the
  active option, guarded with optional chaining because jsdom lacks the method.
- **Wording and state.** The no-match copy was a context-free "No results". It
  now names the query, matching the settings and context variants. While doc
  bodies are still fetching, an empty list read as "no match"; a `loadingBodies`
  flag now shows "Loading results…" for that window.
- **Duplicate titles.** Rows were keyed by `kind + title`, so two tasks with the
  same title collided. Keys are now the flattened index, which is unique within
  the list.

Tests: `src/ui-app/tests/command-palette-a11y-qa.test.ts` is a new jsdom suite.
Its ARIA, legend and focus-restore cases are tables over the three scopes. The
scroll, duplicate-title, query-wording and loading cases are single cases.
`keyboard-shortcuts-qa-browser.test.ts` gained a table case that renders the
empty-result palette at each width and audits overflow.

## Approaches tried

I first considered fixing focus in `SearchBar.vue` by passing a ref to its
button. That would have fixed the pill and left the class open for any future
caller that forgets `returnFocusEl`, so I moved the fallback into the overlay.

For the combobox wiring I considered `aria-activedescendant` alone versus a
full combobox role. I used the full pattern, with `aria-expanded` tied to
whether any result is shown, because a bare `aria-activedescendant` on a plain
text input is not announced consistently.

For the loading state I considered a persistent live region announcing result
counts. The repo has no `sr-only` utility and I kept the change small, so I
did not add a live region. Result counts are not announced; that is a possible
follow-up.

## Challenges and blockers

- The first vitest run from the repo root failed with a Vue import-analysis
  error because the UI Vue plugin is only loaded by `src/ui-app/vite.config.ts`.
  Running with `--config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts` fixed it.
- My first loading-state test mounted the overlay with `open: true`. The open
  watcher does not fire for an initial prop, so no body load started and the
  test saw "No results". The test now mounts closed and opens, which matches how
  the header pill uses the component.
- `bun run build` fails at its `vue-tsc` step on errors in components I did not
  touch (`CheckRunsPanel.vue`, `DebuggerChat.vue`, `InputCard.vue`,
  `ModelPlaygroundPanel.vue`, `ChatQueuedNotice.vue`). None of the reported
  errors involve `SearchOverlay.vue` or my tests. I rebuilt the UI with
  `vite build` directly so the WebKit suites had assets; I did not fix the
  pre-existing type errors because they are outside this task.
- The two QA records that describe palette copy, `docs/qa/2026-11-stories-inbox-search-qa.md`
  and `docs/qa/2026-11-keyboard-shortcuts-qa.md`, are read-only (`-r--r--r--`).
  I did not change their permissions. One line in the stories/inbox record still
  calls the empty copy "context-free"; that is now out of date. The keyboard
  record needs a short #1269 section describing these fixes. Both need a human
  to unlock them or a follow-up edit.

## Key learnings

- Fixing a focus or label bug at one caller leaves the class open. The palette
  is shared by three scopes and an unknown future caller, so the fallback and
  the ARIA wiring belong in the component.
- `useId()` is the Vue-native way to make ids unique across the several palette
  instances mounted on different routes. I used it rather than a module counter.
- jsdom lacks `scrollIntoView`; any test that exercises highlight movement needs
  either a stub or optional chaining in the component.
- The first scoped check failed in the remote gate's typecheck: `mount` and
  `setProps` in my new test were typed from the `.vue` shim and rejected `open`.
  The fix routes mounts through one typed helper and casts `setProps` to the
  real prop shape. The rerun of the scoped check passed.
- Watchers on props do not fire for the initial value. Tests that depend on an
  open-triggered side effect should mount closed and then open.
